chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan and al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan and Hammad, from Ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"It is not permissible for the person in ihram to marry, nor to give in marriage; if he marries or gives in marriage while in a state of ihram, his marriage is invalid."

key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.مُحِلاًّ: While in a state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage for a person performing Hajj in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the prohibition on marriage during ihram renders the contract void (*batil*) rather than merely valid but penalized, emphasizing the sanctity of the ritual state. This hadith is central to the jurisprudence of *Hajj* and *Umrah*, illustrating how specific restrictions of ihram suspend normal civil capacities like contracting marriage. The ruling underscores the principle that acts contrary to the core conditions of ihram invalidate the legal effect of the transaction.
